headline_finding.summary: On the clean-only pipeline (RF retrained on n_train=67 physically-valid rows only, evaluated on n_test=24 physically-valid rows only), ML's test R2 collapses to -0.0263 (WORSE than predicting the population mean) and the Ridge stack's test R2 is -0.0482. Onsager physics scores R2=-1.0405 on the same clean test set -- still poor, but the paired bootstrap 90% CI of (physics_MAE - ML_MAE) is [-0.40, +13.92], INCLUDING ZERO: ML's MAE advantage over physics is not statistically distinguishable from chance at this honest sample size. Both pre-registered refute criteria fire. CONCLUSION: the previously-reported large ML-over-physics advantage for dielectric constant (shipped KPI R2=0.64 vs Onsager R2=-1.67) is NOT a robust chemistry-to-property skill signal -- it is an artifact of RF exploiting the LOW VARIANCE of the corrupted majority (962/1075 rows collapsed toward the under-converged electronic-only limit, which is easy to predict near-constant and looks like high R2 against a homogeneous target). On the honest, physically-valid 10.5% of the population, NEITHER physics NOR ML NOR the stack produces a competent dielectric-constant predictor (all three R2 <= 0, i.e. no better than the test-set mean).

That leaves the training data still contaminated. Fire 1's own recommended followup #3 was: 're-run ... filtered to the physically-valid subset only, to determine whether the shipped ML KPI's reported MAE/R2 are themselves inflated ... by training against corrupted labels.' This fire executes exactly that.
